reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: Section 19.1 gives the professional/workmanlike services warranty measured against industry standards, 19.2 gives a 90-day Deliverable conformity warranty running from the later of delivery or acceptance plus hosted Services conformity for the entire subscription term (equal to or better than the 12-month software benchmark), and 19.3 adds compliance with Applicable Law and a no-malicious-code warranty.

Section 19.4 supplies the required remedy ladder (prompt re-performance, repair or replacement at no charge, escalating to termination and refund of Fees) and is expressly non-exclusive for fraud, infringement, confidentiality, privacy, security and indemnified claims, so the remedy is real rather than illusory.

Section 19.5 disclaims only implied warranties and expressly states that no disclaimer limits an express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so the disclaimer does not swallow the express warranties.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or comment is proposed and the rendered paragraphs are unchanged from the originals.

The failed deterministic check is a false negative from the regex: the period is written out as "ninety days" rather than a numeral or a month/year unit, which is a phrasing variant that still satisfies the ≥90-day threshold. The narrowing of the malicious-code warranty to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor" is a common market qualifier and does not warrant downgrading to a deviation.
